subject: Novacore Health — on-prem cluster install profile and IO/network constraints
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novacorehealth.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: ops@novacorehealth.com
Date: 2029-07-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment — site constraints and initial requirements

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We discussed moving forward with a private on-prem deployment in our Boston colo (MA1). Before we lock dates, the ops team asked for a short write-up of our constraints so your field team can size the cluster and identify any design gaps. High level items below — attaching a site inventory we pulled together.

- Expected production workload: steady 80 rps inference, spikes to 300 rps for 5–10m at peak. Mostly 2–4k token context windows.
- Model mix: primary model will be a 13B open model (fp16), fallback to a 7B quantized variant for low-priority requests.
- Node goals: want predictable 200ms p95 for single-stream requests; can tolerate 30–60s for long-batched jobs.
- Storage: need 70TB usable for persistent datasets (block store, encrypted), plus ephemeral NVMe on nodes for KV cache. Retention policy: user data kept 30 days, logs 90 days.
- Networking: private VLANs per tenant, BGP to our edge, NAT for outbound to patch servers. Egress to third-party APIs must be auditable.
- Security: we require customer KMS (HSM backed) and SOC2 evidence for audit trail.
- Power and rack constraints: racks are 20A circuits; we may be limited on per-rack PDUs.

Attachment: novacore_site_inventory.xlsx (site inventory + switch uplinks).

Can your team confirm recommended node profiles (CPU/GPU mix), persistent blockstore options, and any caveats around our 20A per-rack limit?

Best,
Samir
Ops Lead — Novacore Health

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novacorehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2029-07-23T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — site constraints and initial requirements

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear summary and the inventory sheet. I reviewed the attachment and the high-level constraints look reasonable. Quick responses up front, and then I captured a short plan for a technical preflight workshop.

- Node profiles: initial recommendation is a mixed fleet — "inference" GPU nodes (2x A10 / equivalent per node, 96GB host RAM) for the 13B model and a smaller CPU+quantized GPU pool for the 7B fallback. We can provide exact GPU families once we confirm available hardware in your racks.
- Storage: we recommend encrypted blockstore (44–60 IOPS/TiB baseline for metadata-heavy workloads) for persistent datasets and local NVMe (ephemeral) for KV cache. We'll propose a caching layer to keep steady p95s under 200ms.
- Networking: prefer a dedicated VLAN with BGP peering to avoid hairpinning; MTU 9000 recommended if your switching fabric supports it.
- Power: 20A/rack is tight if you want dense GPU nodes. We can spread GPU nodes across more racks or offer a hybrid with some nodes colocated in a denser rack in our partner colo.

Proposed next steps (short workshop agenda):
1) 60-minute preflight (field + infra): review rack-level constraints, switch ports, uplink capacity, and PDU map.
2) Detailed node profile review: confirm GPU family and host memory.
3) Storage and retention: map blockstore to your backup plan and KMS integration.
4) Network routing and egress audit requirements.

Are you available for a preflight on Thu 2029-07-25 10:00–11:00 EDT? If not, propose two slots. I'll bring Marissa (deployment PM) and Karthik (infra lead) to the call.

Attachment: redwood_site_questionnaire.docx (I'll send a short questionnaire in a follow-up).

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novacorehealth.com>, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2029-07-24T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — site constraints and initial requirements

On Wed, Jul 24, 2029 at 11:03 AM Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Samir — thanks for the clear summary and the inventory sheet.

Quick technical notes from the deployment planning perspective — attached is a candidate-nodeprofile.csv (simple CSV with example node types and expected per-node throughput). Key assumptions below:

- Inference node (A10-equivalent): 1 GPU per node, expected steady throughput ~30–40 concurrent single-streams; p95 ~150–220ms depending on context window.
- Cache topology: local NVMe per node (1–2TB) with periodic sync to blockstore for checkpoints. We expect ~20% cache hit rate initially; we can tune pre-warming to improve this.
- Persistent blockstore: recommend iSCSI/FC-backed block with encryption at rest (we will integrate with your KMS). Use LVM volumes for PVs; set QoS on volumes for hot tiers.
- Snapshot strategy: daily incremental snapshots, weekly full; retention 30/90 as requested. Snapshots stored in your offsite archive (we'll coordinate the backup topology).

Risk callouts:
- Rack power: if only 20A circuits are available per rack, we will need to limit GPU density to 1 GPU/node or increase rack count — both affect network and cross-rack traffic.
- Egress auditing: for outbound calls to external APIs, we will add transparent proxying and per-route logging — this needs an egress IP plan.

Attachment: candidate-nodeprofile.csv

Action: If you can share preferred GPU SKU or allowed instance list, we will finalize node counts and produce per-hour cost/throughput trade-offs for the call.

—Marissa
Sr. Deployment PM — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novacorehealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2029-07-24T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — site constraints and initial requirements

Folks — adding a few networking and routing specifics to consider before the preflight:

- BGP peering: prefer iBGP to your edge routers with a static prefix advertisement for the cluster egress IPs. We will request 2 /27s for service egress (can be smaller if NAT is used).
- MTU: 9000 recommended, but confirm end-to-end (switches, TOR, and uplinks). If jumbo frames are not supported, we will adjust the KV cache packetization.
- Firewall/NAT: we need deterministic egress for auditability. Recommend a small pool of egress IPs per environment and route only those through an auditing proxy.
- Cross-rack traffic: with spread-out GPU nodes, NVMe-local caching will reduce cross-rack bandwidth, but expect more inter-node traffic for model KV syncs. Provision at least 25Gbps uplinks per rack if GPUDensity > 2 nodes/rack.

Operational ask: please provide switch model + firmware and PDU outlet map in the site inventory before the workshop so we can sketch a cabling/placement plan.

Karthik
Staff Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
